diagnosis: The image shows an extremely over-jammed core: roughly 750 tightest pairs are tied at the maximum cosine to within a few times \(10^{-16}\), while most points have 15–35 contacts. Against this, exactly one point has zero contacts, a few have only about 4–6, and others have up to 38, so the configuration is missing a balanced, fully jammed structure in which every point participates comparably and can carry positive equilibrium stress. The loose rattler is essentially decoupled from the rigid core that determines the score, and neither tangential LP steps nor generic shakes can improve that core without breaking many simultaneous contacts; small perturbations fall back into the same basin and large ones destroy the packing. The contact graph projected onto its principal axes also shows no obvious symmetric orbit or cluster structure to exploit, and recent programs have compounded the problem by running long anneals plus final LP polishing beyond the 180-second limit, losing any intermediate result.

One point is a rattler with zero contacts, so its degrees of freedom are wasted while hub points are heavily over-constrained; the missing structural property is a balanced, equitably stressed contact graph, plausibly arising from a more symmetric configuration, rather than this lopsided rigid graph. Consequently tiny shakes plus LP polishing return to the same basin, and larger shakes are not repaired within the allotted optimization. Repeated worker programs also implement similar basin-hopping and then exceed the execution limit, so only the initial \(4.6\times10^{-8}\) LP improvement has actually scored.

diagnosis: The best code is a fully jammed, over-tight local optimum: roughly 750 pairs are tied at the maximum to machine precision, so any small tangent move raises some contact and the LP can only recover the same point. It is not equi-tight or balanced: contact degrees range from 0 to about 38, including one rattler with no contacts and one with only a few, while overloaded hubs and PCA-projected clusters carry the maximum. That rattler/void coexisting with crowded hubs is the missing structural property—an optimum should have nearly regular contact degrees, every point attaining the global maximum, and an isotropic covariance close to \(I/13\). Repeated basin-hopping has therefore mostly re-entered the same basin, while recent workers also timed out because they ran many 1000-step relaxations and full LPs without a hard global anytime deadline.
